The Process Technologist is the site subject-matter expert for manufacturing processes, process capability and scale-up. The role combines hands-on production support with structured process improvement and technical project execution. 
How your agenda looks like: - Maintain and expand relationships with customers - Analyze and optimize production processes to improve efficiency, quality, and throughput - Drive continuous improvement initiatives across manufacturing operations. - Lead the transfer of new products and formulations from R&D to Production - Troubleshooting & Root Cause Analysis - Support capital investment projects and participate in factory improvement projects - Improvements of production performance 
Your team: 
You will report to the SHEQ Manager and work closely together with the Operations, R&D and Engineering Team in Goes. 
What makes you a great fit: - Education: Bachelor's degree (BSc) in Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, Chemistry or a comparable discipline; master's degree is an advantage - Work Experience: At least 5 years of relevant experience in process technology, process engineering or manufacturing engineering within the chemical, adhesive, coatings, formulation-based or comparable process industry - Technical skills: Mixing, rheology/viscosity, pumping, dosing, scale-up, process validation and production equipment. - Project skills, Digital skills, Analytical and Stakeholdermanagement - Local language: Y, preferable Dutch and English Bolton Adhesives is a Business Unit of Bolton that supplies innovative gluing, bonding and sealing products.

Intern 
 Posted on Sep 22, 2026 
Deploy detailed models of coupled ocean / sea ice processes, probe their turbulent interactions, compare with observations, and design parameterizations for global climate models. 
Job description 
The past decades have been associated with substantial losses of sea ice over both hemispheres. Existing climate models are currently unable to accurately forecast these changes, in part due to their imperfect representation of ocean and sea ice interactions at sub-grid scales. 
This project aims to improve our physical understanding of these fine-scale processes, including the melting and breakage of sea ice, using a framework consisting of an ocean Large Eddy Simulation (LES) and a Discrete Element Model (DEM) of sea ice. Results from these simulations will be validated against a combination of in-situ and remote sensing data from both the Arctic and Antarctic sea ice regions. Based on this new understanding, the candidate will develop parameterizations that can emulate these physics for use in more coarsely-resolved climate models. 
This fully-funded position is part of the European Research Council (ERC) 'ICE-FLOE' project, and will involve collaborations with other team members at TU Delft and internationally. There may also be the opportunity to assist with a research cruise in Antarctica.
